clue.text: Rotund, he crams odd stocking this December, at the end merry?

definitions.text: Rotund, he crams odd stocking this December, at the end merry?

indicators.note: something odd is strange or out of order, so the letters around it are to be rearranged
points to the closing letter of the month named just before it

blocks.note: rotund means plump
taken as written, ready to be rearranged
taken as written, held inside the rearranged letters
the final letter of the month

explanation.surface: A stout, jolly figure stuffing a stocking in December: the whole clue describes him.
explanation.walkthrough: FAT is followed by HERCHRISTMAS, a rearrangement of HE CRAMS with THIS and R tucked in ('stocking' them). The whole clue doubles as a portrait of FATHER CHRISTMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa is traditionally plump and jolly, filling children's stockings on Christmas Eve late in the year.

clue.text: Fellow provided The Beano regularly for rugby team?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the comic's name is taken

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow
provided that means if
first, third, fifth and seventh letters; the Beano is a British children's comic

explanation.surface: Someone supplied a comic for the rugby players to read.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union side fields fifteen players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: One causes distress to teacher? That's about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier words wrap around the letter for right

blocks.note: taken as written
a mentor is a guide or teacher
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone suggests that a teacher is the one who causes distress, and agrees with the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's about right' sounds like casual agreement, but it tells you the preceding words go around the letter for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is a person who inflicts suffering or anguish on another.

clue.text: Treat ham making comeback to prime part of Toby Belch?

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word for preserving meat is read from its end
the prime part is the first, so just the opening letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: to cure ham is to treat it by salting or smoking
the initial letter of the name

explanation.surface: Sir Toby Belch, the Shakespeare drunk, sees his ham being prepared again.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Toby Belch is the carousing knight in Twelfth Night; his surname here is the definition, so 'Toby' only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An eruct is an old-fashioned or formal word for a burp, the noise of wind escaping from the stomach.

clue.text: He should be paid honour by soldiers

blocks.note: credit means praise or honour
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A man ought to be saluted and honoured by the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'paid honour' as one phrase; the definition stops at 'paid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is someone owed money, so a debt to him must be settled.

clue.text: A bit of bacon for a sheriff's sandwiches

indicators.note: to sandwich is to hold between two layers, so the phrase before it holds the answer inside

blocks.note: running across the words from the end of the first to the middle of the last

explanation.surface: A sheriff's sandwiches contain a little bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like a plural noun in the surface but it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a thin slice of bacon, a single portion cut from the side.

clue.text: Celebrity's carrying one luggage item for flight

indicators.note: the celebrity holds the next item within, as one carries a load

blocks.note: a star is a celebrity; the 's means 'is'
Roman numeral one
a case is a suitcase

explanation.surface: A famous person is lugging their own bag onto a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: STA(I)R then CASE. 'Flight' suggests air travel to suit the luggage, but it means a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a run of steps between floors, which is what a staircase provides.

clue.text: One island or another rejecting new court authority?

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing out, so the letter for new is removed

blocks.note: another island: the Isle of Man
N is the abbreviation for new
the Lawn Tennis Association governs British tennis courts

explanation.surface: One island or a second refuses to accept a fresh ruling from the judiciary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court authority' suggests a judge; it is the body running tennis. The Isle of Man sits in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is a Mediterranean island nation lying south of Sicily.

clue.text: Crowning ascendant English monarch's matter involving millions

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the letter for millions goes inside the assembled string
in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the whole string is turned round

blocks.note: E abbreviates English
M is the abbreviation for million
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
pus is matter discharged from a wound

explanation.surface: A rising English sovereign's business concerns a vast fortune at the coronation.
explanation.walkthrough: E, M, ER and PUS line up as EMERPUS, which, written upward, gives the answer. 'Matter' is the medical sense, yellowish discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowning as an adjective means topmost or highest, like a crowning achievement, the same as supreme.

clue.text: Metal band Iron Maiden leaving obstinate sort outside car

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter for maiden goes out of the following word

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
RR is Rolls-Royce
M is a maiden over in cricket scoring
a mule is a stubborn person

explanation.surface: A heavy-metal group's lineup, with Iron Maiden walking out and a stubborn member waiting outside in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Iron Maiden is a heavy-metal band, so 'Metal band' looks like a description of it; the band splits into iron and maiden. What is left of MULE stands outside, after, the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferrule is a metal ring or cap fitted round the end of a stick or handle to strengthen it.

clue.text: Dish will turn heads, touring California

indicators.note: to turn something is to flip it round, so the word for heads is read backwards
touring means travelling around, so the turned word goes round the state abbreviation

blocks.note: polls is an old word for heads
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A glamorous dish will make people stare while travelling around California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' as an attractive person suits 'turn heads', but it is the culinary sense. Poll for head survives in 'poll tax'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scallops are shellfish served as a dish, and also give their name to a shallow baking dish shaped like their shell.

clue.text: Make a choice, wanting leader?

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word goes without its opening letter

blocks.note: to select is to make a choice

explanation.surface: Voters choosing someone because they lack a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The same three words both define and supply the word that loses its first letter; a leaderless group would also elect a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to choose, whether by vote or as a personal decision between options.

clue.text: Special beer in a tin mostly gets you drunk

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the container word loses its final letter
a special version is made differently from usual, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, shortened

explanation.surface: A can of strong beer will get you drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets you drunk' reads as a verb phrase, but 'drunk' alone is the noun definition, a drunk person.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a habitual drunkard, a person who is often intoxicated.

clue.text: Swimming race takes a short time

indicators.note: takes means admits or holds within, so the word for race receives the next letters

blocks.note: a race of people, a nation
A as written plus T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A swimming race is won in very little time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming race' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'Swimming' alone and 'race' means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: Natation is the formal, Latin-derived term for the act or skill of swimming.

clue.text: Actor, initially no great shakes, gathering rising support

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the first letter of the following word counts
shaking jumbles things up, so these letters are mixed
in a down entry rising means written upward, so the word for support reads backwards
gathering means taking in, so the mixed letters wrap around the turned word

blocks.note: first letter
taken as written, to be mixed
aid means help or support

explanation.surface: A performer who was mediocre at first is now winning more backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No great shakes' is an idiom for mediocre, but it splits into N, GREAT and an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles, or a writer of tragedies.

clue.text: Salt is healthy when limiting it

indicators.note: limiting means setting bounds around, so the word for healthy encloses the pronoun

blocks.note: hale means robustly healthy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Salt is good for you as long as you keep your intake down.
explanation.definitionFit: Halite is the mineral name for rock salt, naturally occurring sodium chloride.

clue.text: One con man is busted – he won't get off easily

indicators.note: busted means broken, so these words are smashed and reassembled

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A swindler is caught by police, and he is not going to escape lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get off' sounds like escaping punishment; here it means getting off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: An insomniac struggles to fall asleep, so drifting off never comes easily to him.

clue.text: Chap spies Virginia first of all in European city

blocks.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia
Len is a man's name
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A man catches sight of Virginia first, in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of all' moves VA to the front of LEN and CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a major port city on Spain's eastern coast.

clue.text: Riot could possibly result in heartless massacre

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letters are removed from the following word
a possible result suggests the letters may be reworked into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A disturbance might turn into a slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the middle SA from the eight letters leaves six to rearrange. 'Riot' reads as unrest but means something hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech a riot and a scream are both very funny people or events.

clue.text: Engaging engineers, band made CD from score?

indicators.note: engaging means taking on or holding, so the band surrounds the engineers

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
a squad is a band or group

explanation.surface: A group hires sound engineers and produces a CD of its music.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUA(RE)D. A score is twenty and CD is Roman 400; twenty times itself is four hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplying a number by itself is squaring it, and twenty squared equals four hundred.

clue.text: One has fine teeth, the judges observed

blocks.note: a panel of judges
saw means observed

explanation.surface: The judges noticed someone with a lovely smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine teeth' suggests a beauty contest, but they are small cutting teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel saw is a carpenter's handsaw with small, closely spaced teeth for cutting thin boards.

clue.text: Wikileaks maybe has leak about British model

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for leak goes round the next pieces

blocks.note: leak and wee are both slang for urinating
B abbreviates British
to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: The whistle-blowing outfit has a leak concerning a British fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leak' fits Wikileaks perfectly, but it is the slang for passing water.
explanation.definitionFit: Wikileaks is an example of an online site publishing documents.

clue.text: Overlook counterfeit tenners at first

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so only the opening letter of the banknotes word counts

blocks.note: to forge is to counterfeit
first letter

explanation.surface: Someone ignores forged ten-pound notes.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something is to neglect or fail to notice it, much as one fails to remember.

clue.text: Where ensign may be in a predicament?

blocks.note: first meaning: a flag is hoisted to the top of a mast
second meaning: British slang for being in trouble

explanation.walkthrough: An ensign is a flag. 'Up the pole' is British slang for in difficulty, or crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag flies at a flagstaff's top, and the same idiom informally describes someone stuck in a mess.

clue.text: One's nicked maybe? One's nicked certainly

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who may be arrested, 'nicked' being British slang for arrested
second meaning: someone who has stolen, 'nicked' being slang for stole

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves read the same; 'One's' is 'one is' in the first and 'one has' in the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber may well be arrested by police, and by definition has already taken goods.

clue.text: Disband extremely disruptive crowd

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the two end letters are kept

blocks.note: the outside letters
a mob is an unruly crowd

explanation.surface: Break up a very unruly crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Demob is short for demobilise, releasing troops from service.
explanation.definitionFit: To demobilise an army is to stand down its troops and send them home.

clue.text: Derek excavated fort to discover pottery

indicators.note: dug out means the inside is removed, leaving only the shell of the word

blocks.note: Del is a short form of Derek
the outside letters

explanation.surface: An archaeologist named Derek digs at a fort and finds pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excavated' suits the dig but means emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is tin-glazed earthenware, often blue and white, named after the Dutch town where it was made.

clue.text: Using abusive language gets band into trouble? The opposite

indicators.note: into means going inside, which sets up one word sitting within another
the opposite flips the stated arrangement, so the outer and inner words swap roles

blocks.note: a ring is a band
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Someone's swearing lands their pop group in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the band goes into the trouble; 'The opposite' flips that, so the trouble goes into the band: R(AIL)ING.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain bitterly or rant, so railing describes angry, scolding speech.

clue.text: Sculptor and composer given mimimum initial advance

indicators.note: the opening letter moves up the alphabet by the smallest step, one place

blocks.note: Vincenzo Bellini, Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: An artist and a musician receive a small upfront payment.
explanation.walkthrough: B moves on one letter to C. 'Advance' looks like money paid ahead, but it is moving forward in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini was a Renaissance goldsmith and sculptor, famed for his bronze Perseus in Florence.

clue.text: Maybe the truckie finally can reverse his vehicle stuck in narrow pass

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of the driver word is kept
to reverse a vehicle is to back it up, so the word for can is read backwards
stuck in means jammed inside, so the pieces sit within the word for a narrow pass

blocks.note: a defile is a narrow gorge
a tin is a can
last letter; a truckie is a lorry driver
an artic is an articulated lorry

explanation.surface: A lorry driver tries to back his truck out of a tight mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe the' means the word 'the' is an example of the answer. Artic is British shorthand for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite article, so it is one example of the class.
